title: Zaire
capsule: Zaire was the name given to the Democratic Republic of the Congo by President Mobutu Sese Seko in 1971 as part of his 'authenticité' campaign to replace colonial and Western place names with African ones; our dataset's from-date of 1973 reflects the period of full institutional consolidation under that name. Mobutu ruled as a one-party kleptocratic dictator for over three decades, nationalizing foreign mining assets, suppressing political opposition, and accumulating a personal fortune estimated in the billions while state infrastructure collapsed. The First Congo War (1996–97), backed by Rwanda and Uganda, swept Laurent-Désiré Kabila's forces from the east to Kinshasa; Mobutu fled in May 1997, and Kabila renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Zaire's external borders as a recognized state are clearly established through treaty and UN records; internal provincial boundaries and areas of effective government control versus rebel/secessionist zones in the 1990s are less precisely represented in the geometry.
